original_test_intent: Verify the approved inter-VLAN isolation policy by demonstrating that SUT and peer on distinct tags cannot ping or transfer the approved test artifact in either direction when routing/ACL policy requires denial.
original_method: After engineering fixes the intended policy, configure or verify identity-locked endpoints on distinct VLANs, capture switch/router/firewall state, run bounded bidirectional ping and harmless transfer-denial attempts, then restore temporary state.
manual_activity: Engineer/network owner decides routing/ACL authority and approves distinct VLAN topology and negative-test method; agent executes only the bounded approved policy checks.
required_inputs: DUT/peer parent/bond and distinct VLAN IDs/tags/trunks
Approved harmless transfer protocol/port/artifact and denial evidence
Management isolation, OOB/console, rollback/recovery and invalid-run rules
safety_requirements: Do not assume distinct tags imply denial; verify authoritative policy first
Exclude management/production paths and preserve switch/router/firewall baseline
Use bounded probes and harmless non-sensitive transfer attempts
Stop on unexpected reachability, isolation breach, route/ACL drift or access loss
Restore only approved temporary state; never auto-delete unrelated rules or files
agent_execution_scope: Run bidirectional bounded ping and approved transfer allow/deny tests
Record complete policy-correlated evidence and restore temporary state
Do not choose expected policy, modify unrelated rules, expose data, auto-retry/recover or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Define expected routed or isolated behavior and authoritative policy surfaces
Approve test topology, artifact and recovery
Review results against policy and issue PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Conceptually recognizes policy dependence but is incomplete and unsafe: sample topology, one endpoint and one ping cannot satisfy bidirectional ping and file-denial criteria.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Verify approved distinct-tag endpoints and routing/ACL/firewall state, then run bounded ping and harmless transfer checks in both directions against the explicit policy.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Different VLANs, both ping directions, both file-copy directions, expected failures and 5/0 timing fields are preserved pending policy authority.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute a policy-anchored, bidirectional isolation matrix with complete network-control-plane and endpoint evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds authoritative policy, safe negative-test artifacts, exact mapping and rollback.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No direction or file-denial criterion is dropped while the expected outcome remains pending.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Routing, VRFs, ACLs, firewall state and proxy/overlay services can intentionally permit or block traffic independently of VLAN IDs.

project_override_considerations: If routing is intentionally allowed, engineering must revise/split acceptance at the review layer while preserving the Master conflict; the reviewer cannot label that behavior a DUT failure by assumption.
expected_evidence: Bidirectional harmless transfer allow/deny results with protocol errors and no data leakage
Cleanup/restoration, logs, security disposition and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master mandates failure solely from different VLAN IDs, but configured inter-VLAN routing or ACL policy may intentionally permit traffic; authoritative policy is missing.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Static review is complete and policy can be decided later without stopping subsequent review.

review_improvement: Anchors the negative test to real routing/security policy and restores every bidirectional ping and transfer checkpoint.
independent_technical_reasoning: VLAN tags separate L2 broadcast domains, but an L3 router, VRF leak, firewall or proxy can intentionally connect them. Therefore reachability is a policy property, not a consequence of different tag numbers alone, and both directions plus application transfer must be checked against the declared controls.
